ref: Spirtes, Glymour, Scheines. Causation, Prediction, and Search, 2nd ed., MIT Press, 2000
claim: Constraint-based algorithms such as PC and FCI recover causal structure from conditional-independence tests only up to an equivalence class, and only under assumptions such as faithfulness (and, for PC, causal sufficiency); FCI drops causal sufficiency and outputs a partial ancestral graph.

ref: Chickering. Optimal structure identification with greedy search. JMLR 3, 2002
claim: Greedy Equivalence Search (GES) searches over Markov equivalence classes with a score and is consistent in the large-sample limit.

ref: Reisach, Seiler, Weichwald. Beware of the Simulated DAG! Causal Discovery Benchmarks May Be Easy To Game. NeurIPS 2021 (arXiv 2102.13647)
claim: In commonly used simulated benchmarks the marginal variance tends to increase along the causal order (varsortability), so a baseline that sorts variables by variance and regresses matches continuous-optimisation methods on raw data, while those methods fail after standardisation.

ref: Reisach, Tami, Seiler, Chambaz, Weichwald. A Scale-Invariant Sorting Criterion to Find a Causal Order in Additive Noise Models. NeurIPS 2023 (arXiv 2303.18211)
claim: A scale-invariant analogue, R2-sortability (sorting by the coefficient of determination), is also high in default simulation settings and can be exploited by a simple baseline.

ref: Kitson, Constantinou. The impact of variable ordering on Bayesian network structure learning. Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery 2024 (arXiv 2206.08952)
claim: The order of the columns in the input file alone changes the graph that score-based hill climbing learns, by more than a large increase in sample size does.

ref: Brouillard, Squires, Wahl, Kording, Sachs, Drouin, Sridhar. The Landscape of Causal Discovery Data: Grounding Causal Discovery in Real-World Applications. CLeaR 2025 (arXiv 2412.01953)
claim: A review of causal-discovery papers finds that the Sachs protein-signalling data is the only real dataset in a large share of real-data evaluations, that its ground truth is not definitive, and recommends evaluation on interventional data.

ref: Li, Liu, Wang, Ye. CausalArena: Benchmarking Causal Discovery in the Foundation Model Era. arXiv 2609.11897, 2026
claim: CausalArena is a benchmark of synthetic, semantic (named, story-based) and formula-grounded structural causal models with observational and interventional exports and a public leaderboard of causal-discovery methods.

ref: Chevalley, Roohani, Mehrjou, Leskovec, Schwab. A large-scale benchmark for network inference from single-cell perturbation data. Communications Biology 8, 412, 2025 (arXiv 2210.17283)
claim: CausalBench evaluates gene-network inference on genome-scale Perturb-seq data from the K562 and RPE1 cell lines, scoring predicted edges on held-out interventional data with a mean Wasserstein distance and a false omission rate.

ref: Replogle et al. Mapping information-rich genotype-phenotype landscapes with genome-scale Perturb-seq. Cell 185(14), 2022
claim: The CausalBench data come from genome-scale CRISPRi Perturb-seq screens.

ref: Kiciman, Ness, Sharma, Tan. Causal Reasoning and Large Language Models: Opening a New Frontier for Causality. arXiv 2305.00050 (TMLR 2024?)
claim: Large language models answer pairwise causal-direction questions about named variables with high accuracy on existing benchmarks, and part of that benchmark is memorised by the models.
